text:
mike: FYI rolling BMC+BIOS update started for eu-west GPU racks (canary -> phased). I'm seeing ~18 nodes enter OOB and ~6 report secure-boot toggled to 'required' during the flash. Provisioner is failing those nodes on PXE + sigverify.

infra-bot: [deploy-runner] firmware-rollout bmc-eu-west canary=10% -> paused due to node failures: https://internal.ops/run/1765551234 :warning:

sara: Confirmed. Nodes are in 'oob-locked' state — IPMI present but UEFI reports mismatch. Provisioner attempts = 3, retries = 0, queue backlog +22 for gpu pools. We can't reprovision these without a rollback or toggling secure-boot acceptance.

tanvi: We already diverted some jobs to west-us. If this stays degraded we'll start billing on-demand replacements and cross-region egress will spike. Rough ballpark +$1.5k/hr if we keep 20% of traffic diverted.

dario: Quick triage: stop the rollout expansion, push a temporary policy to allow legacy-unsigned images for reprovision, then schedule a controlled rollback for the affected nodes. Patch commands:
```
# pause rollout (internal tool)
opsctl fw-rollout pause --id bmc-eu-west --reason "oob secure-boot failures"
# allow legacy for reprovision (short term)
provisioner config set --region eu-west --allow-unsigned-boot true --ttl 1h
```

oncall-ops: Running the pause now. Also kicked remediation script to attempt IPMI powercycle + clear NV variables on the 18 nodes (tracked in the remediation job). Current progress: 6/18 cycled, 2 reprovisioned successfully (no secure-boot enforcement), 10 still pending.

sara: Can we avoid toggling global allow-unsigned? Prefer a per-node override so we don't broaden the attack surface. If we must, set a very short TTL and audit events. Also let's rate-limit the provisioning queue - it's hammering the registries.

mike: Agreed on per-node override. I'm running the per-node job now for the 18 nodes. Also pausing the canary expansion and setting rollout to manual.
```
opsctl node-override set --nodes @eu-west-gpu-affected --accept-unsigned true --reason "emergency reprovision" --expires 1h
opsctl fw-rollout set --id bmc-eu-west --mode manual
```

infra-bot: opsctl: rollback request received, nodes targeted: 18, action: node-override applied (6 success, 12 pending).

dario: Also pushed a temporary routing adjustment to keep jobs from hitting reprovisioned nodes until they report healthy. We'll reroute to west-us / capacity-fallback pool and mark eu-west GPU pool as degraded -12%.

tanvi: Please annotate expected cost delta in the ticket. Based on current diversion and on-demand fallback, estimate ~USD 2.2k/hr for the next 2 hours if we can't reprovision the rest quickly.

mike: Noted. I'll add the cost estimate to the incident ticket and tag finance. If we don't have the remaining nodes healthy in 30m we'll escalate to incidents channel and open an infra-incident. :triangular_flag_on_post:

oncall-ops: Remediation update @10m: 11/18 nodes cycled, 7 reprovision attempts queued, 3 reprovisioned healthy. Still seeing a small subset with TPM/UEFI state stuck — will try NV var clear + reflash.

sara: Thanks — if TPM is stuck we'll need the deeper rollback (remove secure-boot efivars, reflash bootloader). That path will be noisier but may be necessary for nodes that refuse to reset the flag.

mike: OK. Hold the global policy change, continue per-node overrides and targeted fixes. I'll follow up in 20m with status.

infra-bot: [audit] actions recorded: fw-rollout pause, node-override applied (eu-west), provisioner config change (per-node). Audit link: https://internal.ops/audit/1765551234

mike: tagging #product-ml and #customer-ops about a potential 10-15% capacity hit in eu-west for GPUs until this is cleared.

sara: will post the final reprovision list in the incident ticket once remediation completes.

mike: closing loop for now — keep updates brief in this thread. If anything regresses, escalate to incidents. :thumbsup:
